stages.title: Advanced grammar
explain: The subjunctive (il congiuntivo) is used after verbs of opinion, wish, emotion and doubt: "penso che", "voglio che", "sono contento che", "è possibile che". Forms: "che io parli", "che tu parli", "che lui parli"; for -ere verbs "che io scriva". Irregulars: essere (che io sia), avere (che io abbia), andare (che io vada), fare (che io faccia).

Use the condizionale for polite requests and hypotheses: "vorrei", "potresti". The trapassato prossimo shows an earlier past action: "Era già uscito quando sono arrivato." Choose between passato prossimo and imperfetto: "Ieri ho mangiato" (a completed event) versus "Da bambino mangiavo molto" (a habit).

gq.q: Choose the correct form: Penso che lui ___ ragione.
Why is "Quando ero piccolo, giocavo ogni giorno" in the imperfetto?
o: It describes a repeated habit in the past
gq.why: The imperfetto expresses habits and ongoing past states.

panel.q: Which is the subjunctive of "essere" for io?
What does the trapassato prossimo express?
o: An action before another past action
panel.why: It is the past of the past.

panel.q: Why do "Ieri pioveva" and "Ieri ha piovuto" differ?
o: The imperfetto describes ongoing background, the passato prossimo a completed event

points.ask: When do I use the imperfetto?

teach.model: The subjunctive is used after expressions of opinion, wish, emotion and doubt, like penso che and voglio che. Irregulars include sia, abbia, vada and faccia. The imperfetto expresses habits, and the passato prossimo expresses completed events.

stages.hook: Why does Italian say "Penso che sia vero" and not "Penso che è vero"?
stages.mnemonic: Opinion, wish, doubt, feeling: the congiuntivo is near the heart.

stages.title: Complex sentence patterns
explain: Italian "se" clauses follow patterns. Real possibility: se plus present, then present or future: "Se vieni, sono contento." Imagined: se plus congiuntivo imperfetto, then condizionale: "Se avessi tempo, viaggerei." Impossible past: se plus congiuntivo trapassato, then condizionale passato: "Se avessi studiato, avrei passato l'esame."

Pronouns combine: "Me lo dai?" (Will you give it to me?) uses mi + lo = me lo. The impersonal "si" gives general statements: "In Italia si parla italiano." The passive uses essere or venire: "La lettera è stata scritta da Marco."
items: will you give it to me?
sentences: If I had time, I would travel.
Can you give it to me?

gq.q: Choose the correct form: Se avessi tempo, ___
gq.why: Se plus congiuntivo imperfetto takes the conditional.

o: Se is not followed by the conditional in the condition
gq.why: The conditional goes in the result clause only.

panel.q: What does "me lo" represent in "Me lo dai?"
How does Italian often avoid a passive?
o: With the impersonal or passive si
panel.why: Si parla italiano is a typical alternative.

panel.q: Why can "Se lo sapevo, venivo" be heard in speech?
o: Colloquial Italian replaces the subjunctive with the imperfetto
panel.why: It is common in speech but is not considered standard in writing.

points.ask: How do I form imagined conditions?
How can I avoid the passive?

teach.model: Use se plus present for real conditions and se plus congiuntivo imperfetto with condizionale for imagined ones. Never put the conditional after se. Pronouns combine, like me lo and glielo. Si can replace a passive.

stages.hook: What is the difference between "Se avessi tempo, viaggerei" and "Se ho tempo, viaggio"?
stages.mnemonic: Se + congiuntivo, condizionale: the dream pair.

stages.title: Extended conversations
explain: To react: "Davvero?", "Ma dai!", "Sul serio?" To agree: "Esatto", "Sono d'accordo". To disagree politely: "Non sono del tutto d'accordo" or "Sì, però...". To ask for clarification: "Che cosa intende dire?"
Fillers like "cioè", "insomma", "allora" and "praticamente" structure speech. Gestures also carry meaning, and overlapping speech is normal. Keep it flowing by asking: "E poi?", "Perché?"
sentences: I do not quite agree with you.

gq.why: The softening del tutto makes disagreement polite.
It means that is or I mean.

panel.q: A person overlaps your speech in a lively Italian discussion. What does it often mean?
Which phrase asks for clarification formally?
Why does "Ma dai!" not literally mean "But give!"?
o: It is a fixed expression showing surprise or encouragement
panel.why: Idiomatic phrases have their own meaning.

points.ask: How do I ask what they mean?

teach.model: In Italian conversation react with Davvero or Ma dai. Agree with Esatto and disagree politely with Sì, però. Ask for clarification with Che cosa intende dire? Use fillers like cioè and insomma.

stages.hook: How do you keep a conversation going, disagree politely and ask for clarification in Italian?
stages.mnemonic: Agree, add a "però", ask back: three tools for any chat.

stages.title: Formal and informal registers
explain: Italian has levels of formality. Friends say "tu"; strangers, elders and professional contacts get the polite "Lei" (written with a capital L in letters). In the plural, "voi" is the normal form and "Loro" is very formal. In southern Italy, "voi" is sometimes used for a polite singular.

Informal speech uses shortened forms: "Che fai?", "Dai!", "Figurati!". Formal speech uses "La ringrazio", "Mi scusi", "Potrebbe dirmi...?" Vocabulary changes too: "babbo" and "papà" (informal), "padre" (formal), and "tipo" (casual) versus "persona".
sentences: I don't know where he is.

gq.q: Which sentence is the most formal?
gq.why: The conditional with Lei is formal.

gq.q: Why does choosing the wrong register matter?
o: It can sound rude or oddly stiff
It changes the meaning of numbers

panel.q: What verb form goes with Lei?
panel.why: Lei takes the third person singular.

panel.q: When is "voi" used in addressing one person?
o: In some southern regions as a polite form

panel.q: A student writes "Dai!" in a formal letter. What is the problem?
o: A spoken register is used in a formal text

teach.model: Italian uses tu with friends and Lei with strangers, elders and professionals. Lei takes the third person singular. Casual speech uses short forms like Figurati; formal speech uses La ringrazio and Potrebbe.

stages.hook: Why does an Italian teen say "Hai fame?" but a hotel receptionist says "Ha fame?"
stages.mnemonic: Tu for friends, Lei for the world, and the register for the room.

stages.title: Reading articles and literature
explain: Italian journalism often uses the passato prossimo for events, the imperfetto for background and the present for headlines. Passive structures and nominalisation (turning verbs into nouns) make the text dense: "Il governo ha annunciato una riforma" becomes "L'annuncio di una riforma".

In literature, Dante Alighieri wrote the "Divina Commedia" in the fourteenth century, Alessandro Manzoni wrote "I promessi sposi", Italo Calvino wrote "Le città invisibili", and Primo Levi wrote "Se questo è un uomo". Reading strategy: find the topic sentence, identify connectors such as "tuttavia" and "infatti", and notice the tone.

gq.why: Dante wrote it in the early fourteenth century.

gq.q: Why does a news article often use nominalisation?
o: It packs information into fewer words
gq.why: Turning verbs into nouns condenses text.

panel.q: What does "infatti" signal in a text?
o: Confirmation or explanation of the preceding idea

panel.q: Why is Dante important for the Italian language?
o: His Tuscan writing helped shape the literary standard
panel.why: Tuscan became the basis of standard Italian partly through Dante, Petrarch and Boccaccio.

panel.q: Why must a reader identify the narrator's point of view?
o: It shapes what is reliable or biased

points.ask: What do I notice in literature?

teach.model: In an Italian article, read the headline and lead first. Look for connectors like tuttavia and infatti. Notice tense: passato prossimo for events, imperfetto for background. In literature, identify the narrator and tone.

stages.hook: How is an Italian newspaper article different from a short story?
stages.mnemonic: Headline, lead, details: read in that order.

stages.title: Essay and correspondence writing
explain: A formal letter opens with "Gentile Signora," or "Egregio Signor Rossi," and closes with "Cordiali saluti" or "Distinti saluti". An informal letter opens with "Caro Paolo," or "Cara Maria," and closes with "Un abbraccio" or "A presto".
An essay has an introduction, development and conclusion. Use connectors: "innanzitutto", "inoltre", "di conseguenza", "invece", "in conclusione". Avoid repeating words and keep sentences clear.
sentences: I am writing to ask for information.
On the other hand, prices are high.

gq.q: Which opening suits a formal letter to a woman you do not know?
gq.why: Gentile is the standard formal opening.

gq.q: Why do formal letters use Lei pronouns like "Le scrivo"?
gq.why: Lei, with its object forms, marks respect.

panel.q: Which connector introduces a contrast?
panel.why: Invece means on the other hand.

panel.q: Which is the correct opening for a letter to a woman friend?
Why must an essay conclusion not add a new argument?
o: It should summarise and answer the question

points.ask: How do I open to a friend?
What do I use in essays?

teach.model: A formal Italian letter begins with Gentile or Egregio, states its purpose and ends with Cordiali saluti. Friends are addressed with Caro or Cara. An essay has introduction, development and conclusion linked by connectors.

stages.hook: How do you begin and end a formal letter in Italian when you cannot write "Dear" or "Yours sincerely" directly?
stages.mnemonic: Formal letter: greeting, purpose, request, formula.

stages.title: Translation fundamentals
explain: Good translation preserves meaning, not word order. Translate "It's raining cats and dogs" as "Piove a catinelle" (literally "it rains by the basins"), not as "Piove gatti e cani". Beware of false friends: "attualmente" is not "actually" (which is "in realtà").

Watch for structural differences. English "I'm 20" becomes "Ho venti anni". The English "-ing" has no direct equivalent: "I like swimming" becomes "Mi piace nuotare". English "I like it" uses piacere, where the thing liked is the subject: "Mi piace" means it pleases me. Choose between literal, free and idiomatic translation depending on purpose.

gq.q: Why is "Piove gatti e cani" a bad translation?
o: It translates words, not the idiom's meaning
gq.why: Idioms must be replaced by an equivalent expression.

panel.q: What does "attualmente" mean in a translation of "currently"?
How is "I like pizza" best translated?
panel.why: In piacere the thing liked is the subject.

panel.q: Why do translators sometimes change sentence structure?
o: To sound natural in the target language

teach.model: Translate meaning, not word for word. Watch false friends such as attualmente and idioms such as piove a catinelle. Notice structural differences: English -ing becomes an infinitive, age uses avere and like uses piacere.

stages.hook: What is the best translation of "It's raining cats and dogs" into Italian?

stages.title: Regional varieties and cultural context
explain: Standard Italian is based on Florentine Tuscan, but Italy has many regional languages and dialects such as Sicilian, Neapolitan, Venetian and Piedmontese. Regional Italian also varies in accent: a Milanese and a Roman use the same standard words but pronounce them differently, and "anguria" (north) and "cocomero" (centre) both mean watermelon.

Italian is an official language in Switzerland, where it is spoken in Ticino. It is also spoken in San Marino and Vatican City, and by communities abroad in Argentina, Brazil, Australia and the USA. The unification of Italy in 1861 and later television helped spread the standard.

gq.q: Which dialect forms the basis of standard Italian?
gq.why: Standard Italian developed from Florentine Tuscan.

gq.q: Why do different regions have different words for the same fruit?
gq.why: Local usage persists despite a shared standard.

panel.q: Where is Italian an official language outside Italy?
o: Switzerland, San Marino and Vatican City
panel.why: Italian is official in Switzerland and San Marino, and used in Vatican City.

panel.q: What helped spread standard Italian after 1861?
o: Schooling, military service and later television
panel.why: Mass institutions and media promoted a common standard.

panel.q: Why is it wrong to call dialects "bad Italian"?
o: They are separate languages with their own histories
panel.why: Many Italian dialects descend independently from Latin.

teach.model: Standard Italian is based on Tuscan. Italy has many regional languages and accents, and words like anguria and cocomero differ by region. Italian is also official in Switzerland and San Marino.

stages.hook: Do people in Sicily, Naples, Milan and Switzerland all speak the same Italian?

stages.title: Structured debates and presentations
explain: A good argument has a claim, reasons and an example. Introduce your position: "Penso che...", "A mio avviso...", "Sostengo che...". Add: "Inoltre...". Respond: "Certo, ma...", "Capisco il suo punto di vista, tuttavia...".
A presentation has an opening, three parts and a conclusion. Use a clear voice and signposts: "Innanzitutto", "Poi", "Per concludere". End by thanking the audience: "Grazie per l'attenzione."
items: capisco il suo punto di vista
sentences: I think school should start later.
Of course, but the facts are different.

gq.q: Which phrase answers an opponent politely?
gq.why: Certo, ma concedes a point before replying.

gq.q: Why does a speaker use signposts like "innanzitutto"?
o: They help listeners follow the structure

panel.q: Which mood follows "Penso che" in careful Italian?
panel.why: Verbs of opinion such as pensare che normally take the subjunctive.

panel.q: How does a speaker end a talk politely?
panel.why: It is a standard formal closing.

panel.q: Why include an example in an argument?
o: It makes a claim concrete and testable

points.ask: How do I state a position?
How do I structure a talk?

teach.model: State your position with a mio avviso or penso che. Support it with reasons and examples. Answer opponents with certo, ma. Use signposts like innanzitutto and per concludere, and thank the audience.

stages.hook: How do you structure a short debate speech in Italian and respond to the other side?
stages.mnemonic: Claim, reason, example, then reply with "certo, ma".
